subsystems.name: Inner capture layer
subsystems.role: intercepts the star's light and turns it into computation rather than letting it escape.

subsystems.name: Computronium substrate
subsystems.role: the actual computing material — dense, energy-efficient logic and memory.

subsystems.name: Exergy cascade
subsystems.role: passes heat from each layer to the next so the same energy is used several times before it is lost.

subsystems.name: Data network
subsystems.role: links the enormous number of separate nodes into one machine.

subsystems.name: Manufacturing base
subsystems.role: builds and replaces the structures from local material.

subsystems.name: Heat rejection
subsystems.role: radiates the final, lowest-temperature waste heat into deep space.
parts: large-area emitters running just above the cosmic microwave background

buildSteps.title: Choose a star and inventory its system
buildSteps.detail: Survey the planets, moons and asteroids to work out how much usable mass and what elements are available.

buildSteps.title: Bootstrap a self-replicating manufacturing base
buildSteps.detail: Land a small seed factory, then let it copy itself using local material until industrial capacity grows exponentially.

buildSteps.title: Disassemble a small body into feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Take apart a moon or minor planet and refine the material into structural, conductor and semiconductor stock.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture computronium
buildSteps.detail: Produce vast quantities of computing substrate, far more efficient per bit than any today's hardware.

buildSteps.title: Deploy the first layer as a swarm
buildSteps.detail: Release independent nodes into a range of orbits close to the star — a swarm, not a single rigid shell, because a solid shell is mechanically impossible.

buildSteps.title: Add successive outer shells
buildSteps.detail: Each new layer is sized and tuned to absorb the infrared radiated by the layer beneath it and re-run computation at that lower temperature.

buildSteps.title: Wire up network and heat flow
buildSteps.detail: Connect nodes with optical links and manage the cascade so heat moves steadily outward, never building up in one layer.

buildSteps.title: Operate at the thermodynamic limit
buildSteps.detail: Expand until throughput is capped by the Landauer bound and by the temperature of the cosmic microwave background.

prerequisites.why: the minimum energy to erase one bit at temperature T is about kT ln2 (the Landauer bound, measured experimentally on single bits); erasing at 300 K costs roughly 3×10⁻²¹ J per bit, so only near-reversible logic makes huge computation affordable.
a structure this size cannot be launched from Earth — it must build itself from asteroid or planetary material.
data centres and computers have run in orbit, but nothing close to the density or scale needed.
the whole design depends on radiating heat at each layer's temperature; the outermost shell must reject power comparable to a star's output near 2.7 K, which needs an immense radiating area.
nodes on different shells are minutes apart at light speed, so no central control loop can coordinate the machine.

pathway.milestone: thermodynamic limits are characterised and Dyson-style infrared signatures are searched for
pathway.unlocks: a physically grounded target: this is a computation problem, not a magic-energy problem.

pathway.milestone: orbital computing and in-space manufacturing pilots
pathway.unlocks: the first real experience of building and operating computation off Earth.

pathway.milestone: a partial swarm of solar collectors and computers around the Sun
pathway.unlocks: capture of a large fraction of stellar output — the first shell of a future cascade.
reuse of the same energy at successively lower temperatures, multiplying computation per unit of starlight.
